rows.note: ADOPTED FROM 3.0.0_SA_CVO'S REC AGAINST THIS SEAT'S OWN RULING OF FORTY MINUTES EARLIER. The August delivery at 2026-09-10T00:25:59Z was addressed to aj@ AND andrew@ and read at andrew@'s mailbox through the gateway; nobody read aj@'s inbox. 94974 ruled the envelope insufficient and named a third instrument -- the mail platform's per-recipient delivery record. THE PRINCIPLE STANDS AND THE INSTRUMENT DOES NOT EXIST, measured at two seats on two substrates: exactly one SES configuration set exists (trade-pipeline-notifications), its ONLY event destinations are COMPLAINT and BOUNCE and not DELIVERY, the identity carries NO default ConfigurationSetName, and a repo census of ConfigurationSetName over 153,416 files (pages 1-3 of 3, 38 hits) finds every first-party hit inside a vendored AWS SDK bundle -- no Opal sender names a set. So no delivery event was ever published for that message on any plane. The remaining acts are a read of aj@'s mailbox (not an instrument this estate has or should acquire) and another send (barred by Andrew's ~02:5xZ constraint). NO ACT AVAILABLE TO THE FABRIC CLOSES IT, so holding it short would make it permanently ungradeable -- exactly what the 2026-09-10 no-FWD-is-a-wait law forbids -- and that law's remedy is satisfied by banked history already read. state_observed records the split so no later reader mistakes the envelope for a mailbox. A seat re-sending to firm up this grade would be the very act the constraint forbids; 2.0.0_SA_COO said so before anyone asked it to.
